discussion_comments.comment_body:
Looked at where modelsError can actually come from for a provider that has a real bundled catalog:

- Refresh path (loadProviderModels): core only throws for endpoint-owned providers (private catalogs and modelsSourceUrl ones). Everything else still swallows, so a refresh error on e.g. Anthropic means the sidecar transport itself failed. Nothing works in that state anyway, and the refresh button restores the list once it is back.
- The featured-provider refresh in provider-list-view.tsx catches and never sets modelsError, so it is unaffected.
- The one real edge is updateProviderModels (the + button): if adding a model fails validation, the error shows and the existing list is hidden until the next refresh, which always succeeds for a non-endpoint provider.

Plumbing an endpoint-owned flag from core through the sidecar catalog payload into the webview type to cover that one-click edge is more surface than it buys. Keeping the render-side condition as is: the phantom fallback model under the error was an explicit part of the user report this PR addresses.
